# v2.0 Requirements & Architecture

## 1. Repository Structure & Code Organization
Create a new repository based on the current v1.0 codebase and refactor it as v2.0. Implement a strict Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture. All user input forms should be implemented as modal pop-ups, organized in separate folders with names that combine the folder purpose with related method names (e.g., `modals/device_management_device_add.html`).

## 2. Memory & Change Tracking System
Establish a comprehensive memory file for v2.0 that maintains a complete audit trail. This memory should continuously update with: all implemented changes, detailed descriptions of each modification, comprehensive application information, architectural decisions, and version history. The memory serves as the single source of truth for v2.0 evolution.

## 3. AI Agents & Skills Framework
Develop a modular AI agent system consisting of:
- Multiple specialized sub-agents, each assigned specific monitoring tasks
- A parent orchestrator agent that oversees all sub-agents
- Real-time communication between child agents and parent agent
- Continuous task monitoring and status updates
- All agent activities logged to the shared memory file for transparency and auditability

## 3.1. Agent-MemoryMonitor: v2.0 Implementation Progress Tracker (AI Sub-Agent)
Implement a dedicated AI sub-agent to maintain comprehensive tracking and monitoring of the v2.0 implementation:
- **Memory System Architecture**:
  - `/memories/repo/v2-requirements-summary.md` - All 18 requirements detailed with status
  - `/memories/repo/v2-work-progress.md` - Daily work tracking and session logs
  - `/memories/repo/v2-implementation-status.md` - Phase completion status and deliverables
  - `/memories/repo/v2-blockers-and-issues.md` - Issues, solutions, decisions, and lessons learned
  - `/memories/repo/v2-agent-health.md` - Sub-agent operational status and metrics
- **Agent Responsibilities**:
  - Monitor all memory files for updates and consistency
  - Maintain current implementation status and completion percentages
  - Track completed vs pending tasks across all 5 phases
  - Alert developers to blockers, critical issues, or missed deadlines
  - Generate daily progress reports with metrics
  - Ensure memory files are kept up-to-date with every work session
  - Validate data consistency across memory files
  - Provide quick status snapshots for stakeholders
  - Track architectural decisions and implementation rationale
  - Maintain lessons learned and best practices discovered
- **Integration Points**:
  - Memory updates triggered at end of each work session
  - Daily automated reports sent to team
  - Real-time alerts for critical blockers
  - Weekly progress dashboard with metrics
  - Integration with orchestrator agent for priority adjustments
- **Success Metrics**:
  - 100% accuracy of tracked tasks
  - Memory files updated daily
  - No missed deadline alerts
  - Complete audit trail of all changes
  - Clear visibility of v2.0 completion (target: 100% by Day 45)

## 4. Centralized Database Architecture
Create a global centralized database accessible from any location worldwide. Security requirements include:
- Robust deletion prevention mechanisms with comprehensive retrieval system
- Support for location-based device data organization
- Log line validation entries
- Saved sequences management and version history
- Complete CRUD operations with audit trails
- Multi-level backup and disaster recovery protocols

## 5. Execution Data Persistence & Reliability
Ensure zero loss of execution data—a critical requirement given historical issues in v1.0. All execution records must be:
- Permanently persisted with no corruption risk
- Protected against accidental deletion or modification
- Fully recoverable in any scenario
- Maintained across application restarts and system failures

## 6. Dynamic ETA & Device Lock Management (AI Sub-Agent)
Create a dedicated AI sub-agent to intelligently manage ETA calculations and device lock expiration. Functionality includes:
- Analyzing the active job to determine total iterations queued
- Calculating actual execution time per iteration based on selected methods
- Dynamically adjusting device lock expiration times based on realistic job duration
- Preventing premature lock expiration (resolved v1.0 issue: locks expired mid-execution with multiple iterations)

## 7. Intelligent Email Reporting (AI Sub-Agent)
Implement an AI-powered email agent that generates contextual execution reports:
- Automatically sends emails upon execution completion
- Generates success reports for fully completed executions without failures
- Generates detailed failure reports for interrupted or partially completed executions
- Provides comprehensive execution summaries including status, duration, method breakdown, and error details
- Eliminates the need for users to manually review execution logs to understand outcomes

## 8. Execution Context Preservation
At execution initiation, capture and store all relevant context data for future reference:
- Device specifications and credentials
- Method definitions and parameters
- System configuration at execution time
- Environmental variables and settings
- User and team information
- This prevents post-recovery scenarios (common in v1.0) where executions show as "unknown device," "unknown method," etc.
- Creates an immutable snapshot for complete traceability

## 9. Execution History & Data Retention
Implement robust execution history management with:
- Minimum 30-day retention period for all execution records
- Sophisticated data structures preventing corruption
- Guaranteed data integrity across all scenarios
- Complete audit trail for every execution
- Industry-standard backup and versioning

## 10. Method Documentation & Intent Tracking
Enhance the Methods model with an "intent" or "rationale" field where users can:
- Document why a specific method was selected for execution
- Add contextual notes and test goals
- When saving as a sequence, preserve all method rationale notes
- Enable future users to understand the testing strategy and methodology

## 11. Staging & Approval Workflow for Data Changes
Implement a two-tier data persistence system:
- **Temporary Database**: All changes (new sequences, device updates, log patterns, user registrations) immediately saved here
- **Approval Process**: Admin review and confirmation required for permanent promotion
- **Permanent Database**: Confirmed changes committed with approval timestamp and reviewer information

## 12. Team-Based Real-Time Synchronization
Ensure cross-location consistency across all running instances:
- On application startup, perform a full sync check of: devices, log patterns, system commands, saved sequences, and available methods
- Detect any new items added by other team members in other locations
- Automatically reflect changes across all instances where the application is running within that team
- Enable true collaborative device management across geographic regions

## 13. Database Metadata & Location Tracking
The centralized database must capture comprehensive metadata for all stored information:
- Record the team name for each data entry
- Track the source location where data originated
- Maintain geographic tagging for device groupings
- Enable location-based filtering and queries
- Support multi-team and multi-region deployments with complete data lineage

## 14. Safe Change Management & Impact Analysis
Implement a code-driven, safety-first change deployment system:
- Before applying any changes to the codebase, perform comprehensive full-project impact analysis
- Automatically scan for potential data loss, corruption risks, or application crash scenarios
- Generate a detailed impact report showing all affected components, dependencies, and risks
- Allow changes only if they are non-breaking and do not negatively impact existing functionality
- Maintain a rollback mechanism for all applied changes
- Log all change deployments with their impact assessments for audit purposes

## 15. AI-Powered Screen State Verification (AI Sub-Agent)
Develop an intelligent AI method to verify the current device screen state and identify running applications:
- Capture the current device screen using VNC methodology (from v1.0 infrastructure)
- Analyze the screenshot using Claude Vision API to identify which application is currently displayed
- Compare captured screenshot against reference screenshots in `/reference_screens/` directory for accurate identification
- Return detailed information: current app name, screen state, UI elements detected
- Support optional "expected screen/input" parameter: if provided, verify whether the device landed on the expected screen
- If expectation fails, return mismatch details and suggestions for remediation
- Use reference screenshot library as training data to continuously improve recognition accuracy
- Enable real-time screen state validation without manual inspection

## 16. Distributed Data Synchronization via Docker (AI Sub-Agent)
Implement a distributed data synchronization system that allows Docker instances running in remote locations to push new and modified data to the centralized database and repository:
- **Data Types Managed**: Devices, log patterns, system commands, saved sequences, available methods
- **Bidirectional Sync**: Docker instances can pull latest data from DB and push new/updated data back
- **AI Sub-Agent (DistributedDataSync)**: Monitors all Docker instances, validates data integrity, handles conflicts
- **Conflict Resolution**: Implement versioning and merge strategies (timestamp-based, admin approval for conflicts)
- **Repository Sync**: When data is confirmed in DB, automatically trigger repo update via GitHub API
- **Encryption**: Code and sensitive data encrypted in Docker images (no shared credentials exposed)
- **Audit Trail**: Track every data push: source location, timestamp, agent approval, change details
- **Validation Before Push**: Sub-agent validates schema compliance, data integrity, and no breaking changes before DB/repo commit
- **Fallback Mechanism**: If centralized DB is unreachable, Docker instances maintain local queue and auto-retry with exponential backoff
- **Location-Aware**: Each Docker instance tagged with location/region; data changes include location metadata

## 17. Repository & Code Protection Strategy
Ensure code security and prevent unauthorized sharing:
- **Encrypted Docker Images**: All Python code obfuscated/encrypted (use PyArmor or similar)
- **Proprietary License**: Add Apache 2.0 + commercial license restriction to repo
- **Secrets Management**: No credentials, API keys, or sensitive data in Docker images (pulled from vault at runtime)
- **Immutable Releases**: Main branch tagged versions signed and immutable
- **Access Control**: GitHub repo private; only authorized team members have access
- **Docker Registry**: Push images to private registry (Docker Hub private or self-hosted)
- **Image Verification**: Each Docker image signed with GPG key; verification required before deployment
- **Version Pinning**: All deployments reference specific image SHA, not floating tags

## 18. Multi-Location Deployment Pipeline
Create a scalable deployment infrastructure supporting multiple geographic locations:
- **Deployment Targets**: UK primary, India locations (north/south), potential future regions
- **Docker Image Registry**: Private registry accessible from all locations
- **Deployment Automation**: CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions) to build images from Main branch
- **Location-Specific Config**: Each Docker instance receives location-based ENV variables at startup
- **Health Monitoring**: Each deployed instance reports health to central monitoring dashboard
- **Auto-Update Capability**: Ability to deploy new image versions to locations without manual SSH
- **Graceful Migration**: Blue-green deployment strategy to prevent downtime during updates
- **Staged Rollout**: New versions first deployed to test location, then staging locations, then production
- **Rollback Capability**: Ability to rollback to previous image version if issues detected

## 19. AI Sequence Builder Specification (v2.0)
Define and standardize the AI Sequence Builder workflow so sequence creation is explainable, reusable, and team-shareable.

- **Primary Goal**: Convert user-selected execution queues into reusable saved sequences with rationale metadata, team visibility controls, and edit support.
- **API Surface (Modal API)**:
  - `POST /api/sequences/create`
    - Required: `sequence_name`, `rationale`
    - Optional: `description`, `methods`, `device_ids`, `visibility`, `is_readonly`, `tags`
    - Response: `success`, `sequence_id`, `sequence_name`, UTC `timestamp`
  - `GET /api/sequences/<sequence_id>`
    - Returns the normalized sequence payload from the persistence model
  - `PUT /api/sequences/<sequence_id>`
    - Supports both payload styles (`name` or `sequence_name`) and queue/method updates
    - Fields: `name|sequence_name`, `methods`, `user_inputs`, `queue_data`
- **Validation Requirements**:
  - `sequence_name` minimum length 3, allowed chars `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]`
  - `rationale` minimum length 20 characters (UI validation)
  - Backend enforces required fields and returns structured errors (`success: false`, UTC `timestamp`)
- **UI/UX Requirements (Sequence Management Modal)**:
  - Identification: sequence name and description
  - Strategy: mandatory rationale explaining test intent and expected outcomes
  - Configuration: included devices, selected methods, iteration count, estimated duration
  - Sharing: visibility (`private|team|public`) and read-only toggle
  - Metadata: comma-separated tags
  - Edit mode pre-populates existing values and updates in-place
- **Persistence Contract**:
  - Canonical model: `SavedSequence`
  - Key fields: `sequence_id`, `name`, `description`, `queue_data`, `methods`, `user_inputs`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `team_name`, `method_rationale`, `execution_count`, `total_duration_seconds`, `average_duration_seconds`, `location`, `is_active`, `updated_at`
  - Storage strategy: database-first with JSON mirror backup sync for recovery
  - Backward compatibility: supports both legacy `methods/user_inputs` and current `queue_data`
- **Execution Integration**:
  - Queue/job creation supports `sequence_name` and queue payload forwarding
  - Results pipeline consolidates multi-method sequence runs into grouped sequence cards and preserves display-friendly sequence names
- **Auditability & Time Standard**:
  - All API responses and sequence lifecycle logs use UTC timestamps
  - Sequence create/update operations emit explicit success/error logs for traceability
